en: O Śaubhrarāja, O Rājarāja, [I bow to Him] who is honored by the lotus-born Brahmā, eternally worshipped by His devotees, and praised by those who worship Sudhanvan;
who is resplendent with a lotus, a discus, the Kaustubha gem, and a sword, and who wields the mace.
I take refuge in the abode of Campakāpurī, which is not merely a dwelling place.

I bow to the one who wears the enemy of serpents as a garland, who reclines upon the king of excellent serpents, whose lotus-like eyes are dear to the enemy of lotuses (the moon), who possesses four arms,
who causes the destruction of those born from mud, and who nourishes those not born from mud.
I take refuge in the abode of Campakāpurī, which is not merely a dwelling.
To the leader of all the worlds, the bestower of desired objects, the breaker of Śiva’s bow, the ender of the arrogant Rāvaṇa,
the wearer of yellow garments, and the giver of rags to the naked one.
I take refuge in the dwelling of Campakāpurī, which is not merely a dwelling.
He who is worshipped by Nārada and others; he who has shattered the mountain of men and women (the demon Naraka);
he whose forebody was born from the abode of Nara;
he whose dwelling is the finest of women; and he who is the abode of the destroyer of evil men.
I take refuge in the dwelling of Campakāpurī, which is not merely a dwelling.
He who has the color of a dark cloud, who grants liberation at will, who brings about the end of Time, who casts far away the noose of evil times,
and who is the sun amidst the multitude of lights of the sovereign jewel-armored body.
I take refuge in the residence of Campakāpurī, which is not merely a dwelling.
The destroyer of the teacher of Dakṣa, the shatterer of the eyes of Kuhu and Aṭakā,
served by the songs of the Yakṣas, uniquely consecrated for the protection of the gods,
the slayer of the host of Akṣa, and the savior with a glance from his side-long look.
I take refuge in the abode of Campakāpurī, which is not merely an abode.
He whose broad chest is adorned with a stone necklace strung with golden threads, who is colored by various jewels, who is distinguished by his mace, who is the source of compassion,
who wears a blazing crown, and upon whom the triple mark (tripuṇḍra) shines brilliantly.
I take refuge in the residence of Campakāpurī, which is not merely a dwelling.
I bow to the Lord of Indirā, who is imperishable and free from all ailment; whose broad orb of an autumnal moon is eclipsed by the beauty of his face; whose teeth are like jasmine buds;
whose waist shines with a girdle of tinkling bells brightened by his gentle smile.
I take refuge in the dwelling of Campakāpurī, which is not merely a dwelling.
